angle: Concept drift, distribution shift, cross-dataset generalization, open-world/open-set issues in traffic classification and NIDS, and stability of explanations under drift

papers.title: Transcend: Detecting Concept Drift in Malware Classification Models
papers.authors: Roberto Jordaney, Kumar Sharad, Santanu K. Dash, Zhi Wang, Davide Papini, Ilia Nouretdinov, Lorenzo Cavallaro
papers.relevance: Seminal conformal-evaluation framework that detects concept drift by computing per-class p-values from non-conformity measures instead of trusting classifier confidence, founding the rejection-based drift-detection line all later security-drift work builds on.

papers.title: TESSERACT: Eliminating Experimental Bias in Malware Classification across Space and Time
papers.authors: Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Roberto Jordaney, Johannes Kinder, Lorenzo Cavallaro
papers.relevance: Shows published malware-classifier results are inflated by spatial and temporal bias (training on future data), introduces time-aware evaluation constraints and the AUT metric that temporal-degradation studies now use as standard.

papers.title: Transcending TRANSCEND: Revisiting Malware Classification in the Presence of Concept Drift
papers.authors: Federico Barbero, Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Lorenzo Cavallaro
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
papers.relevance: Formalizes and extends Transcend's conformal rejection (TRANSCENDENT), showing classification-with-rejection generalizes across malware domains and classifiers as a principled defense against drifting inputs.

papers.title: CADE: Detecting and Explaining Concept Drift Samples for Security Applications
papers.authors: Limin Yang, Wenbo Guo, Qingying Hao, Arridhana Ciptadi, Ali Ahmadzadeh, Xinyu Xing, Gang Wang
papers.relevance: The key drift+XAI hub: contrastive-autoencoder latent distance detects drifting samples and a distance-based perturbation method explains WHICH features caused the drift, directly linking drift detection to explanation.

papers.title: Enhancing State-of-the-art Classifiers with API Semantics to Detect Evolved Android Malware (APIGraph)
papers.authors: Xiaohan Zhang, Yuan Zhang, Ming Zhong, Daizong Ding, Yinzhi Cao, Yukun Zhang, Mi Zhang, Min Yang
papers.relevance: Shows classifier 'aging' under malware evolution and slows it by encoding API semantic similarity, cutting retraining frequency and labeling effort on a 7-year, 320K-app dataset - the canonical semantic-feature answer to drift.

papers.title: Continuous Learning for Android Malware Detection
papers.authors: Yizheng Chen, Zhoujie Ding, David Wagner
papers.relevance: Hierarchical contrastive learning plus uncertainty-based active learning to keep a detector alive over seven years of drift, cutting false negatives from 14% to 9% versus best prior continual-learning baselines.

papers.title: INSOMNIA: Towards Concept-Drift Robustness in Network Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Giuseppina Andresini, Feargus Pendlebury, Fabio Pierazzi, Corrado Loglisci, Annalisa Appice, Lorenzo Cavallaro
papers.relevance: First major drift-mitigation framework for NIDS proper: semi-supervised incremental adaptation with nearest-centroid label estimation, and uses explainability-based feature-importance analysis to interpret how the model evolves under drift.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection in the Open World: Normality Shift Detection, Explanation, and Adaptation (OWAD)
papers.authors: Dongqi Han, Zhiliang Wang, Wenqi Chen, Kai Wang, Rui Yu, Su Wang, Han Zhang, Zhihua Wang, Minghui Jin, Jiahai Yang, Xingang Shi, Xia Yin
papers.relevance: Detects, EXPLAINS, and adapts to normality shift (benign-side drift) in DL anomaly detection unsupervised, reducing labeling overhead and validated on long-term NIDS/log data plus a SCADA deployment - the detect-explain-adapt loop for the benign class.

papers.title: AnoShift: A Distribution Shift Benchmark for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
papers.authors: Marius Dragoi, Elena Burceanu, Emanuela Haller, Andrei Manolache, Florin Brad
papers.relevance: Benchmark over 10 years of Kyoto-2006+ NIDS traffic with IID/NEAR/FAR temporal splits, showing consistent performance collapse on FAR years across models from Isolation Forest to masked language models.

papers.title: ReCDA: Concept Drift Adaptation with Representation Enhancement for Network Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Shuo Yang, Xinran Zheng, Jinze Li, et al.
papers.relevance: Recent top-venue NIDS drift adaptation via self-supervised representation enhancement and robust fine-tuning under scarce labels.

papers.title: On Generalisability of Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Siamak Layeghy, Marius Portmann
papers.relevance: Evaluates seven supervised/unsupervised models across four NetFlow NIDS benchmarks and finds no model generalises across all datasets - the clearest single demonstration of the cross-dataset generalization gap.

papers.title: DI-NIDS: Domain Invariant Network Intrusion Detection System
papers.authors: Siamak Layeghy, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Marius Portmann
papers.relevance: Uses domain-adversarial networks (DANN with gradient reversal) to extract domain-invariant flow features and improve cross-dataset NIDS performance - the main domain-adaptation answer to the generalization gap.

papers.title: The Cross-evaluation of Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (XeNIDS)
papers.authors: Giovanni Apruzzese, Luca Pajola, Mauro Conti
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
papers.relevance: First systematic cross-evaluation framework for ML-NIDS over six datasets; shows cross-dataset results collapse relative to in-dataset ones and warns against naive model transfer between networks.

papers.title: Are Existing Out-Of-Distribution Techniques Suitable for Network Intrusion Detection?
papers.authors: Andrea Corsini, Shanchieh Jay Yang
papers.relevance: Tests six OOD detectors from vision/other domains on unknown attacks in NIDS and finds new attacks are not guaranteed to appear OOD, questioning direct transfer of OOD tooling to traffic.

papers.title: Deep learning for encrypted traffic classification in the face of data drift: An empirical study
papers.authors: Navid Malekghaini, Elham Akbari, Mohammad A. Salahuddin, Noura Limam, Raouf Boutaba, Bertrand Mathieu, Stephanie Moteau, Stephane Tuffin
papers.relevance: Tracks two SOTA deep ETC models across ISP datasets collected two years apart: accuracy decays in production, retraining only partially recovers it, and traffic-shape features prove more drift-resilient than TLS-header features.

papers.title: Sustaining the High Performance of AI-Based Network Traffic Classification Models
papers.authors: Jielun Zhang, Fuhao Li, Feng Ye
papers.relevance: Addresses keeping AI traffic classifiers performant as the application mix changes (new/unseen apps), i.e. model sustainability under open-world class evolution in ToN-level traffic classification.

papers.title: CESNET-TLS-Year22: A year-spanning TLS network traffic dataset from backbone lines
papers.authors: Karel Hynek, Jan Luxemburk, Jaroslav Pesek, Tomas Cejka, Pavel Siska
papers.relevance: Year-long backbone TLS dataset (180 services, 100Gbps lines) built explicitly to evaluate classifier robustness against temporal drift in production networks - the main public drift benchmark for traffic classification.

papers.title: Fine-grained TLS services classification with reject option
papers.authors: Jan Luxemburk, Tomas Cejka
papers.relevance: Large-scale (141M flows, CESNET-TLS22) fine-grained service classification arguing the reject option is essential for deployment because training sets can never contain all classes of a dynamic Internet.

papers.title: Drift-Based Dataset Stability Benchmark
papers.authors: Dominik Soukup, Richard Plny, Daniel Vasata, Tomas Cejka
papers.relevance: Proposes a dataset-stability benchmark combining concept-drift detection with ML feature weights, demonstrated on CESNET-TLS-Year22, to predict when deployed traffic classifiers will degrade.

papers.title: Deep Learning and Traffic Classification: Lessons learned from a commercial-grade dataset with hundreds of encrypted and zero-day applications
papers.relevance: Commercial-grade study of DL traffic classification that treats zero-day (unknown-app) traffic as a first-class problem and shows DL feature extraction helps identify unknown classes at scale.

papers.title: Robust Network Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Jun Zhang, Xiao Chen, Yang Xiang, Wanlei Zhou, Jie Wu
papers.relevance: Seminal zero-day traffic work: combines supervised and unsupervised learning (RTC) to identify traffic of applications never seen in training while retaining accuracy on known classes.

papers.title: FlowPrint: Semi-Supervised Mobile-App Fingerprinting on Encrypted Network Traffic
papers.authors: Thijs van Ede, Riccardo Bortolameotti, Andrea Continella, Jaehyun Hwang, Andreas Peter, et al.
papers.relevance: Open-world app fingerprinting without prior app knowledge: builds fingerprints from destination correlations and detects previously UNSEEN apps at 93.5% precision, a core open-world capability prior classifiers lacked.

papers.title: AI/ML for Network Security: The Emperor has no Clothes (Trustee)
papers.authors: Arthur S. Jacobs, Roman Beltiukov, Walter Willinger, Ronaldo A. Ferreira, Arpit Gupta, Lisandro Z. Granville
papers.relevance: The XAI-generalization bridge: global decision-tree surrogate explanations (Trustee) expose shortcut learning, spurious correlations, and OOD vulnerability in published network-security models, showing why in-dataset accuracy fails to transfer.

papers.title: LAMDA: A Longitudinal Android Malware Benchmark for Concept Drift Analysis
papers.relevance: 12-year, 1M+ sample drift benchmark that explicitly quantifies EXPLANATION DRIFT via Jaccard and Kendall distances over SHAP attributions - showing the features a detector relies on shift over time even when accuracy holds.

papers.title: Combating Concept Drift with Explanatory Detection and Adaptation for Android Malware Classification (DREAM)
papers.relevance: Successor to CADE: embeds explanatory drift detection inside a contrastive autoencoder with expert knowledge, achieving equal accuracy with 76.6% fewer newly labeled samples - explanation used as the drift-handling mechanism itself.

papers.title: Online Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems with Explainable Concept Drift Detection and Adaptation Phases
papers.authors: Drago et al.
papers.relevance: Directly on the angle: an online IDS framework whose concept-drift detection and adaptation phases are made explainable, from the group behind several drift-aware IDS systems (HOIDS).

papers.title: Beyond Detection Accuracy: Measuring Explanation Cost, Stability, and Utility for Resource-Aware IoT Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Abdurrahman Tolay
papers.relevance: Measures local explanation STABILITY (TreeSHAP) alongside cost and utility for LR/DT/RF/XGBoost IDS on a leakage-safe CICIoT2023 split; finds RF most explanation-stable while XGBoost shows top-feature turnover and attribution-magnitude drift.

papers.title: Can SHAP-Based Explanations Differentiate Between Concept Drift and Scale Drift in Computer Networks Data?
papers.relevance: Asks the angle's question head-on: under pure scale drift classifier performance degrades while TreeSHAP attribution distributions remain stable, so monitoring SHAP distributions can distinguish drift types in network data.

papers.title: Addressing Concept Drift in IoT Anomaly Detection: Drift Detection, Interpretation, and Adaptation (CDDIA)
papers.relevance: Unified framework that detects drift in IoT streams, INTERPRETS drift points, and adapts the model, aimed at cutting the false positives that unexplained normality changes cause.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Android Malware Detection: Towards Understanding Why the Models Perform So Well?
papers.relevance: Uses XAI feature attributions to diagnose WHY detectors score high under unrealistic (temporally-inconsistent) settings, connecting explanation analysis to experimental bias and temporal drift.

papers.title: OpenCBD: A Network-Encrypted Unknown Traffic Identification Scheme Based on Open-Set Recognition
papers.relevance: Applies open-set recognition (CNN + transformer encoder, three-stage train/test) to flag unknown encrypted traffic classes at inference time.

papers.title: Robust open-set classification for encrypted traffic fingerprinting
papers.relevance: Open-set treatment of encrypted traffic fingerprinting so classifiers reject flows from classes absent at training.

papers.title: Reliable Open-Set Network Traffic Classification
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.relevance: RoNeTC quantifies reliability via uncertainty estimation to make open-set traffic classification decisions trustworthy - uncertainty as an implicit form of self-explanation.

papers.title: TrafficGPT: An LLM Approach for Open-Set Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.relevance: GPT-2-based feature extraction improves open-set traffic-analysis performance about 12.7% over ET-BERT, representative of the pretrained-transformer wave hitting open-world traffic classification.

papers.title: Few-Shot Open-Set Traffic Classification Based on Self-Supervised Learning
papers.relevance: Combines self-supervised pre-training with unknown-discovery strategies for few-shot open-set encrypted traffic classification.

papers.title: MORPH: Towards Automated Concept Drift Adaptation for Malware Detection
papers.relevance: Pseudo-label self-training for neural malware detectors that reduces annotation effort under drift when combined with active learning.

papers.title: Fast & Furious: Modelling Malware Detection as Evolving Data Streams
papers.relevance: Stream-learning view of malware detection over nine years of data; notably updates the FEATURE EXTRACTOR as well as the classifier when drift is signaled.

papers.title: Empirical Evaluation of Concept Drift in ML-Based Android Malware Detection
papers.relevance: Cross-algorithm drift study (nine ML/DL algorithms plus LLMs) finding drift is widespread and that few-shot LLMs do not fully mitigate it.

papers.title: Seamless Website Fingerprinting in Multiple Environments
papers.relevance: Shows website-fingerprinting CNNs lose accuracy when training lacks network-location/client variability and applies domain adaptation to generalize across environments.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Generalization Failure in Lightweight Intrusion Detection Models for IIoT Networks
papers.relevance: Documents cross-domain generalization failure specifically for lightweight IIoT IDS models, extending the XeNIDS/Layeghy finding to the resource-constrained regime.

papers.title: Empirical Analysis of Evasion and Poisoning Against Malware Data Drift Detection
papers.relevance: Attacks drift detectors themselves (evasion and poisoning), showing drift-detection components add a distinct attack surface - relevant to trusting drift explanations.

papers.title: Intrusion Detection in the IoT Under Data and Concept Drifts: Online Deep Learning Approach
papers.authors: Omar Abdel Wahab
papers.relevance: Widely-cited online deep learning IDS that explicitly separates data drift from concept drift in IoT streams and adapts online.

papers.title: Model-Based Explanations of Concept Drift
papers.authors: Fabian Hinder, Valerie Vaquet, Johannes Brinkrolf, Barbara Hammer
papers.relevance: General-ML foundation for 'explaining drift': reduces drift explanation to explaining suitably-trained models via spatial feature change - the methodological toolbox NIDS explanation-drift work borrows.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations of Concept Drift
papers.authors: Fabian Hinder, Barbara Hammer
papers.relevance: First formulation of explaining drift itself in human-understandable counterfactual terms, ancestor of the causal drift-explanation line.

papers.title: Outside the Closed World: On Using Machine Learning For Network Intrusion Detection
papers.authors: Robin Sommer, Vern Paxson
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
papers.relevance: The seminal statement of why ML NIDS underperforms operationally - traffic diversity, the closed-world assumption, and the semantic gap - framing every later drift/generalization study.

papers.title: Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security
papers.authors: Daniel Arp, Erwin Quiring, Feargus Pendlebury, Alexander Warnecke, Fabio Pierazzi, Christian Wressnegger, Lorenzo Cavallaro, Konrad Rieck
papers.relevance: Catalogs ten pitfalls of security ML - sampling bias, data snooping, models trained with access to future information, unrealistic class balance - the evaluation-methodology backdrop for all drift claims.

papers.title: Machine Learning (In) Security: A Stream of Problems
papers.authors: Fabricio Ceschin, Marcus Botacin, Albert Bifet, Bernhard Pfahringer, Luiz S. Oliveira, Heitor Murilo Gomes, Andre Gregio
papers.venue: ACM Digital Threats: Research and Practice
papers.relevance: Positions cybersecurity data as inherently drifting/evolving streams with delayed labels and adversarial pressure, and offers a checklist for drift-aware security ML.

papers.title: Evolving cybersecurity frontiers: A comprehensive survey on concept drift and feature dynamics aware machine and deep learning in intrusion detection systems
papers.authors: Methaq A. Shyaa, et al.
papers.relevance: Main recent survey of drift-aware and feature-dynamics-aware ML/DL for IDS; useful map of detectors (ADWIN, Page-Hinkley, DDM) and adaptation strategies.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Concept-Drift-Resilient Network Intrusion Detection Systems
papers.authors: Mateus Komarchesqui, V. G. D. S. Ruffo, Daniel Matheus Brandao Lent, et al.
papers.relevance: Newest survey dedicated specifically to concept-drift-resilient NIDS, consolidating the 2021-2026 wave.

papers.title: Network Intrusion Datasets: A Survey, Limitations, and Recommendations
papers.relevance: Surveys the NIDS datasets on which all drift/generalization claims rest and catalogs their limitations (staleness, labeling errors, unrealistic traffic) - the data-side reason cross-dataset results collapse.
